questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has amplitude A and angular frequency ω. Max speed is:
questions.explanation: In simple harmonic motion, velocity is maximum when the particle passes through equilibrium. At this point, all energy is kinetic: ½mv²_max = ½kA². Since ω = √(k/m), solving for v_max yields Aω.

questions.question_text: Two waves of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz beat together. Beat frequency is:
questions.explanation: Beat frequency equals the absolute difference between the two frequencies: |260 Hz - 256 Hz| = 4 Hz.

questions.question_text: Photon of wavelength 600 nm — its energy is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using E = hc/λ, where h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s and c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s: E = (4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ × 3 × 10⁸)/(600 × 10⁻⁹) ≈ 2.07 eV. Longer wavelengths correspond to lower photon energies.

questions.question_text: Radioactive isotope half-life 5 years. After 15 years, fraction remaining:
questions.explanation: After 15 years, three half-lives have elapsed (15 ÷ 5 = 3). Each half-life reduces the sample by half, so the remaining fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8.
Young's modulus is stress divided by strain. Stress is force per unit area (ML^-1T^-2), while strain is dimensionless. Therefore, Young's modulus has dimensions ML^-1T^-2.

questions.question_text: In Young's double-slit experiment, fringe width is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d, where λ is wavelength, D is distance to screen, and d is slit separation. Since fringe width is inversely proportional to d, the answer is 1/d.

questions.question_text: A capacitor C charged to V is connected to identical uncharged C. Final V on each:
questions.explanation: When the charged capacitor connects to an identical uncharged one, charge redistributes equally between them since they're identical and in parallel. Total charge Q = CV remains constant, now split between two capacitors, so each holds Q/2, giving final voltage V/2 = (Q/2)/C.

questions.question_text: Lorentz force on a charge q moving at v in magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: The Lorentz force depends on the vector cross product of velocity and magnetic field because the force direction must be perpendicular to both, following the right-hand rule. The magnitude is qvB sin(θ), which simplifies to qvB when v and B are perpendicular, making the vector formulation qv × B the complete and correct expression.
